risks: Low: two conversations with a trained nurse and a follow-up call. Risks are distress when discussing alcohol during an acute episode, pressure to take part felt by detained patients, and disclosure of risk during follow-up calls.
consent: Written informed consent by the named nurse only when the patient is judged to have capacity; detained patients are told that declining has no effect on their care or detention; consent for follow-up calls and text reminders is separate.
data: Screening results and session checklists are held in a study file on the hospital network with a study number; audio recordings are deleted after fidelity rating; follow-up answers are entered directly into the study file.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: detained patients, people who are homeless at discharge, people without a phone and people with limited English are the least likely to be screened, to take part and to be reached. Screening and uptake are reported by detention status and length of stay, interpreters are used for sessions, and a second contact route is agreed before discharge.
effectiveness: The study succeeds if it decides whether a larger evaluation is feasible; it will not claim any effect on drinking.
efficiency: Uses approved nurse time and existing training; no new staff.
costs: Printing, a recording device and nurse time within normal shifts; follow-up calls within normal duties of another ward.
grants: None needed; a positive result would support an application for a comparative evaluation.
partnerships: Community alcohol team (referral and advice), two people with lived experience of admission and drinking (materials and follow-up wording), and the ward's nursing team.
rebPath: Research ethics committee review of the feasibility protocol through the hospital research office, following ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki; the opinion is not yet given, so no patient is approached before it.
limitations: One ward; nurses know they are being observed; follow-up by phone may miss the patients doing worst.
summary: Low-risk study with capacity safeguards, equity reporting by detention status and an ethics opinion still awaited.
